text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Guntis Ulmanis rejected a law on compulsory motor insurance and sent it back to parliament.

- The experts from a Russian-Latvian mixed commission are to meet next week to agree on the agenda of the commission's meetings. The agreement on resuming the work of the commission was reached at a meeting between Russian ambassador Alexander Udaltsov and Minister of Environment and Regional Development Anatoli Gorbunovs.

- Speaking at the Swedish Foreign Policy Institute in Stockholm, British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind expressed the hope that the Baltic States would be among those EU candidate members ready to start admission talks by the end of this year.

- Fatherland & Freedom chairman Maris Grinblats visited the public prosecutor's office to verify allegations by party colleague Oskars Grigs about Prime Minister Andris Shkele being involved in Lata International, which allegedly misused agricultural credits.
- It is still not clear whether the death of a woman in one of Riga's hospitals was caused by Mad Cow disease.
- Daugavpils Textile manufacturer in eastern Latvia has been declared insolvent by a local district court.
